_comment: The official SigNoz MCP server (github.com/SigNoz/signoz-mcp-server),
exposed to agents through aw-mcp-gateway. Runs as this app's own
'mcp' sidecar (see aw-app.json runtime.sidecars) and talks Streamable
HTTP natively — no bridge needed.
This is a TEMPLATE. aw-workspace renders it into mcp.json — the file the
gateway's app-scan actually reads — on every activation and every config
save, resolving ${config.x} against this app's saved settings. Do not edit
the rendered mcp.json: it is overwritten, and the value you want lives in
the app's Settings instead.
These tools turn on automatically: the 'provisioner' sidecar (see
aw-app.json runtime.sidecars) logs into SigNoz with the managed root
account, creates a service account + API key through SigNoz's own
v0.128.0 API, and saves it into this app's own 'signoz_api_key' setting
for you — no manual step, as long as 'Manage the root account from
these settings' is turned on in this app's Settings.
If that switch is off, the provisioner reports 'manual-key-required'
(see contributes.doctor / this app's own 'SigNoz API key provisioning
status' setting) and you're back to the manual flow: open this app's
SigNoz UI, go to Settings -> API Keys, create a Personal Access Token
there — a SigNoz-native credential, NOT this workspace's own API key
(that one only guards the OTLP ingest paths, see
docs/app-workspace-api-auth.md) — and paste it into this app's own
Settings -> 'SigNoz API key'. A manually-pasted key that still
validates is left alone; the provisioner never overwrites it.
While signoz_api_key is empty, the renderer disables this server, and
the gateway serves no SigNoz query tools — deliberately, because an
upstream configured with an unresolved placeholder does not fail loudly.
It connects, gets a 401, and serves zero tools, which looks like a broken
app rather than an empty field.
